status: Observed selected-vehicle six-site hexagonal-head pattern; section dimensions remain inferred

supplement.scope: Same exhibit in2014; front hardware pattern only, not its camouflage finish

observed: Two upper heads, one at either side, and a lower pair form a six-site pattern on the fixed circular flange
The lower-left region is partly occluded by the gun and adjacent armor; its exact visible outline is uncertain
Top-midpoint and bottom-midpoint sites of the old eight-head recipe have no corresponding visible fastener
Visible head outlines are hexagonal rather than domed rivet caps

roundFrontOpening.observed: Dark round opening beside the gun barrel on the moving front ball; function and concealed continuation unverified
roundFrontOpening.scope: Real bore through the retained modeled ball replaces the black disk. Diameter, hidden depth and backing remain inferred; no optical function or complete line through the turret is claimed.

turretSocketOpening.scope: Inferred opening through retained front armor layers, required by the actual moving ball. A prior full-fixed sweep found contact at minus10degrees; no contact exclusion is added. Not a measured historical socket diameter.

limits: Absolute bolt circle, head dimensions and tightness orientation are author estimates, not a museum survey
Threads, hidden shanks, attachment backing and original fastener specification are not established
The partly occluded sixth site follows the observed six-site pattern; it is not a newly revealed internal measurement
Flange diameter, gun/turret proportions and global camera/scale remain unaccepted
The other triangular front feature has not been established as an opening or a sight and remains unaccepted
This museum hardware pattern does not establish the wartime equipment of an individual vehicle at Tengxian
